newsitem.title: USA: No response on second Miami money amnesty.
newsitem.headline: No response on second Miami money amnesty.

text.p: Police gave Miami residents a second chance to return hundreds of thousands of dollars of missing money without risking arrest, but the response was a resounding silence.

A Miami police department spokeswoman said on Saturday evening there were no confirmed reports that any money had been returned, although she noted an unconfirmed report that someone had come forward with small change.
"We were told that someone turned in $2," she said after the early evening expiration of the second amnesty, which had been declared on Jan. 15.

Pending further information, the lack of response meant that an estimated $550,000 was still missing from a Jan. 8 accident in which a Brink's armoured truck carrying an estimated $3.7 million flipped on a highway overpass, sending money pouring onto the highway and down onto the streets of one of Miami's poorest neighbourhoods.
During a 48-hour amnesty immediately after the crash, just two people came forward to return money -- an 11-year-old boy and a mother of six gave back a total of $20.38.
Under terms of the second amnesty, people who took the Brink's loot were allowed to turn it over to the Advisory Board or to police until Saturday evening without facing prosecution.
Two women were arrested last week for trying to use food stamps which had spilled from the truck.
